reflection: How do liquid water and water vapour behave differently?
title: States of Matter
description: Sort everyday examples and exact particle models into solids, liquids and gases.
brief: Classify each example as it is described. The particle pictures are simplified models.

groups.label: Solid
groups.description: Keeps its own shape and volume

groups.label: Liquid
groups.description: Keeps its volume; takes container shape

notes:
Focus: shape, volume and a simple particle model. Compare the same material in different states.

Particle dots are schematic, not to scale; they show arrangement, not actual particle size or colour. All particles move: solid particles vibrate about fixed positions. The gas cards use a particle symbol because these gases are invisible.

Do not confuse visible clouds or steam mist (liquid droplets) with invisible water vapour.

All diagrams and symbols are editable inline SVG.
